Native inference defaults, without app-created greeting rules, automatic thinking budgets or synthetic Fast/Deep/Creative presets. Ordinary typed Chat no longer inherits spoken-reply formatting. Manual settings remain saved across model switches; Auto follows model metadata, sourced recommendations and the selected native runtime.

Corrected MLX runtime selection from checkpoint components. The Qwen3.5 9B vision-language checkpoint now uses mlx-vlm with its required model identifier and selected adapter, rather than the text-only runtime. Decoder-only models retain mlx-lm. Native templates and samplers remain in control.

Fixed a false context-compaction failure caused by an invalid system-only token-count request. On the tested Qwen file, 1,819 tokens of conversation became 691 tokens of inspectable memory plus the recall question, preserving the project, numeric budget, deadline and publishing prohibition. The sample omitted the original currency label, so this is not a claim of lossless summarization. Original history remains available.

Focused checks on the same local Qwen, Llama and MiniCPM files covered replies, code, reasoning and context recall; actual app streaming and cancellation also passed. Qwen Auto identity matched direct native output. The native thinking-On case still exceeded the 60-second diagnostic without a final answer; Llama added an incorrect aside after its correct probability calculation. This release does not claim universal intelligence or Windows GPU performance improvements. Full outputs, timings and limitations are in [the native inference audit](https://github.com/UnnamedCoder-568/Uncloud/blob/main/qa/native-chat-audit-2026-10-15.md).

Validation: 1,086 backend tests passed with three skipped in the isolated release-source archive; 148 frontend tests, five desktop tests, production build, Python lint and release-resource checks passed. Model tests ran sequentially and released their workers; Chrome was not operated.
